replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Mathematics has always felt a bit distant to me. With my vocational diploma, I learned practical skills in my field of work, but numbers and formulas never sparked my passion like they did for my spouse. I prefer understanding the philosophy behind economics instead of getting lost in complex calculations. It's practical enough for daily life, but I keep it separate from my personal interests.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Honestly, yes, quite often. When I see a complicated formula, my heart races. My spouse is very patient, but I still feel overwhelmed by the pressure of getting it right. This anxiety is especially high when I try to help my children with homework. I worry about making mistakes or not understanding enough, which makes even simple problems feel threatening.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: No, I haven't used AI for math learning recently. I am more comfortable with traditional methods and talking things through with people I trust. I am cautious about technology, preferring to focus on my yoga and videogame hobbies instead. The idea of relying on an algorithm to explain concepts feels too impersonal for me, and I worry about losing the human element of learning.
